Editor.problem: Earlier point 1 is only partly fixed. Both trace cases now get three load rounds and TRACE_WAIT=120, but propagation still runs inside fix.sh. The time plan in the header adds up to 920s (90+100+100+130+180+100+100+120) against LIMIT=830. Stage 7 has no budget check before it starts. Its wait loop stops when remaining() drops to 15s, so the propagation case can get a shorter wait than the default case. The default wait can also shrink, because limit=$(cap 180 325). load.py still keeps only the last 3 trace IDs per round (recent[-3:]), not 30. Both cases still print a best-of value of 1 or 2, and joined counts 'of 3' use a fixed denominator, not the number of known traces actually found. When stage 7 doesn't run, HERO_MEASURE prints -1. A 'present' contract accepts -1 as a number.
Editor.fix: Move stage 7 into propagate.sh with its own LIMIT. If it does not run, print services_in_trace_propagation=not_run. Change load.py to record 30 sampled trace IDs per round (for example, every Nth request). Report each case as joined traces / known traces found in Splunk, using the same three rounds and a fixed wait of exactly TRACE_WAIT seconds in both. Do not end either wait early unless the other case uses the same early-exit rule. Keep the best-of value of 1 or 2 only as a secondary line.

Editor.problem: p95_added_ms may not be a median. fix.sh computes it as `p95s load-off.txt | sed -n 2p` minus `p95s load-on.txt | sed -n 2p`. The labels say p95s prints 'per round', which suggests round order. If so, line 2 is the second round, not the median, and the reported overhead is one round's value. Earlier point 3's node CPU request is also open. load.py's node_busy_pct reads /proc/stat on the load node only. Nothing records CPU on the orders and inventory nodes, where OBI's cost actually falls. The README says each round prints 'how busy each node was', and that isn't true as written. The run also doesn't record t3 unlimited mode or the CPU credit balance.
Editor.fix: Sort before taking the median: `p95s file | sort -n | sed -n 2p`. Also print the min and max for each side. During each OFF and ON round, capture `kubectl top nodes`, or per-node /proc/stat from the OBI or collector pods, for all three nodes, and print it next to that round's p95. Print the instance credit specification (`aws ec2 describe-instance-credit-specifications`) so the run shows unlimited mode, or switch to m6i.large.

Editor.problem: Earlier point 4 is fixed in the script but not in the contract. pod_restarts_added still has min_entities 1, although fix.sh emits one value per pod for three pods. Restarts after propagation are printed as plain text, with no HERO_MEASURE and no contract entry. A restart caused by the second value would therefore never be checked.
Editor.fix: Set pod_restarts_added min_entities to 3. Add a measurement pod_restarts_after_propagation (kind failure, op present, min_entities 3). Emit it per pod as HERO_MEASURE: pod_restarts_after_propagation[$pod]=$n from restarts_by_pod pods-obi.txt pods-final.txt.
